newsitem.title: USA: Mass. House debates saving some county governments.
newsitem.headline: Mass. House debates saving some county governments.

text.p: The $18.3 billion budget approved last week by the Massachusetts Senate eliminates all counties, and transfers operation of their registries of deeds and the courts to the state.
But Speaker of the House Thomas Finneran has been skeptical about wiping out the entire structure through the budget. His members have not had a chance to vote on the future of counties.
So Tuesday afternoon, the Counties Committee will again hear a proposal to do away with the county system of government.
The committee has heard myriad like proposals several times this year, with proponents arguing that its few essential aspects would be better handled by the state.

Opponents, however, have maintained that counties are crucial to serving the needs of people who do not have easy access to state government. Most lawmakers tend to agree that county government will soon cease to exist - the only question remaining is in what manner will it be abolished.
Gov. Weld has strongly backed the elimination of county government.
The issue came to a head late last year when Middlesex County, home to Harvard University and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, defaulted on $4.5 million in notes.
